shots.visual_event: Saira watches thirty-six-year-old Rohan lock a small bicycle shop; he wears her silver compass symbol as a faded tattoo.
Rohan notices her across the road and freezes—the exact face from the missing poster he has carried for decades.
Saira starts toward him, but nearby street signs and faces lose detail as the memory debt wakes around her.
shots.dialogue_audio: Maya: “If he remembers you all at once, something else disappears.”

shots.visual_event: Saira steps back into shadow and phones the shop instead, hearing her brother’s voice without claiming her place.
shots.dialogue_audio: Saira: “Did your sister like trains?” Rohan: “She hated goodbyes.”

shots.visual_event: Rohan turns toward the empty street while Saira silently breaks; Meera takes her hand without a speech.
shots.dialogue_audio: Rohan: “Who is this?” Saira: “Someone who found her.”

shots.visual_event: In the archive, Saira adds her own photograph to a board of returned passengers and writes NOT HOME YET beneath it.
shots.dialogue_audio: Saira: “We end the debt first. Then I knock.”

end_card.text: HOME IS NOT THE SAME AS RETURNING
